hints: Remember what each test is really looking for, 2,4-DNPH finds any carbonyl while Tollens is much more picky.
Sort the four structures into aldehyde, ketone, both, or neither by spotting $\text{CHO}$ versus $\text{C=O}$ in the middle of the chain.
You need the one that has a C=O for DNPH but has no aldehyde group left to be oxidised by Tollens.
walkthrough:
**Recall what 2,4-DNPH tests for**

Think of 2,4-DNPH as the carbonyl detector. It gives an orange precipitate with both aldehydes and ketones.

Test rule:
$$\text{aldehyde or ketone} + 2,4\text{-DNPH} \rightarrow \text{orange precipitate}$$

**Recall what Tollens tests for**

Think of Tollens as the aldehyde-only detector. It gives a silver mirror only with aldehydes, because only $\text{CHO}$ is easily oxidised.

Test rule:
$$\text{aldehyde} + \text{Tollens} \rightarrow \text{silver mirror, ketone gives no reaction}$$

**Apply both tests to the structures**

We need DNPH positive but Tollens negative, so we need a ketone with no aldehyde group.

$\text{CH}_3\text{COCO}_2\text{H}$ contains $\text{CH}_3\text{C=O}$, a ketone, plus a carboxylic acid. The ketone reacts with DNPH but cannot be oxidised by Tollens, so this fits perfectly.

options.A: Correct. $\text{CH}_3\text{COCO}_2\text{H}$ (pyruvic acid) contains a ketone carbonyl. This gives a positive 2,4-DNPH test. It has no aldehyde $\text{CHO}$ group, and neither ketones nor carboxylic acids react with Tollens, so Tollens is negative.
options.B: Incorrect. $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CHO}$ contains an aldehyde group $\text{CHO}$. It will give a positive DNPH test and also a positive Tollens test (silver mirror), so it fails the 'does not react with Tollens' condition.
options.C: Incorrect. $\text{CH}_3\text{COCHO}$ contains both a ketone and an aldehyde. The aldehyde part ensures both tests are positive. Students sometimes focus only on the ketone and forget the $\text{CHO}$ will still reduce Tollens.
options.D: Incorrect. $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_3$ is propan-2-ol, a secondary alcohol with no carbonyl group. It gives a negative DNPH test and a negative Tollens test, so it fails the first condition.
